description:
## Scope

What's changed:

As an experiment I've introduced 2 new rate limiters applying to sending emails:
- A global limiter which limits the sending of all emails in Directus. This limiter has a Queue in order to delay emails instead of dropping them if the limit is reached (with configurable queue size). Making use of `redis` if available or memory otherwise. This limiter will be useful to match external email providers limits and not exceed them.
- A flows email operation specific limiter. This limiter behaves like the API ones and will throw errors going into the reject path of the Flow, this could cause dropped emails. I decided to use the Flow ID as key here so one flow hitting the rate-limiter will not affect other flows.

## Potential Risks / Drawbacks

- Both of these are opt-in so should be pretty safe

## Review Notes / Questions

- Would we want the email flow rate limiter to also use a queue?
- Does it make sense to separate the email flow rate limiter based on `flow.id`?
- Do the env defaults I made up make any sense?
- Do the env names make sense?
- Would we want an environment variable to disable the email operation in flows completely?

## Checklist

- [x] Added or updated tests
- [x] Documentation PR created https://github.com/directus/docs/pull/489

----
Fixes: PM-1011

Should these start with `RATE_LIMITER_*` to be consistent with the other rate limiter configuration envs (e.g. global, registration etc)

Assuming we rename the bottom 2,  should we need all these? `RATE_LIMITER_.+` would catch all these
```suggestion
  'RATE_LIMITER_.+',
```
Per testing, the err is not an instance of `Error` and does not enter this block. It results in the following being displayed on limit hit:

Based on testing, this is triggered whenever the points are exhausted, rather than only when the queue is full. While this is expected behavior of `removeTokens`[^1] we should only be throwing our error when the queue is full.

ENV 
```
EMAIL_LIMITER_ENABLED=true
EMAIL_LIMITER_POINTS=2
EMAIL_LIMITER_DURATION=60
EMAIL_LIMITER_QUEUE_SIZE=50
```

[^1]:https://github.com/animir/node-rate-limiter-flexible/wiki/RateLimiterQueue#when-is-removetokens-method-rejected
A potential solution here is to construct a `p-queue` with the provided rate limit and manually check + error if the queue size is reached.

Circling back here, this was a misunderstanding. It works as intended and only errors when the queue is full. The removeToken errors if we attempt to [remove more tokens than points](https://github.com/animir/node-rate-limiter-flexible/blob/3fa25fc3d1d6e9b82e9f609596323e67723a057a/lib/RateLimiterQueue.js#L90) which was not the case here
